subject: 2-Chlorophenothiazine
context: 2-Chlorophenothiazine, which consists of the phenothiazine nucleus without the amine side chains of methylene blue, acts as a direct free-radical scavenger independent of mitochondria and NADH. In the cell-free mitochondrial lysate oxidation assay it significantly reduced DCF fluorescence both with and without mitochondria/NADH, unlike MB which required both. Despite potent nanomolar neuroprotection against glutamate, IAA, and rotenone toxicity, it had no effect on oxygen consumption, anaerobic glycolysis, or the complex I-III electron shunt, and it did not upregulate complex IV expression, revealing a mechanism distinct from MB.

subject: Acetate
context: Acetate is converted intracellularly into acetyl-CoA by ACSS2 and is not membrane-permeable acetyl-CoA itself. Acetate supplementation increases global nuclear acetylation including H3K27ac and induces expression of pro-inflammatory genes including IL6, IL8, IL1B and CCL2 without affecting cell cycle regulators p16 and p21. In mitochondria-depleted senescent cells, acetate increases histone acetylation and partially restores a subset of the mitochondrial-dependent SASP programme. However, acetate-induced SASP gene expression is suppressed by the STING inhibitor SN011, showing that chromatin accessibility alone cannot drive SASP transcription without innate immune activation.

subject: Acetyl-CoA
context: Acetyl-CoA is the obligate donor for protein acetylation, including histone acetylation, a modification associated with chromatin relaxation and increased accessibility to transcriptional machinery. In senescent cells, acetyl-CoA availability determines H3K27ac deposition at SASP gene loci: enhancing acetyl-CoA levels promotes SASP gene expression while depleting it limits the programme. Acetate supplementation, converted intracellularly into acetyl-CoA by ACSS2, increases nuclear acetylation and induces pro-inflammatory genes IL6, IL8, IL1B and CCL2 without affecting cell cycle regulators, linking mitochondrial metabolism to the epigenetic regulation of inflammatory genes.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase) inhibition reduces PL-PUFA levels and lipid peroxidation without altering expression of ACSL4, the acyl-CoA synthetase that canonically drives PUFA incorporation into phospholipids during ferroptosis. After ACase knockdown, ACSL4 protein remained high, indicating that the decrease in PL-PUFAs is driven by reduced supply of saturated/monounsaturated fatty acids for Lands-cycle exchange (due to decreased ceramide lipolysis) rather than by changes in ACSL4. Both ACase and ACSL4 knockdown protect senescent cells against RSL3, but through supply-side versus incorporation-side mechanisms respectively.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: The anti-ferroptotic protection conferred by acid ceramidase (ACase) knockdown is independent of the GPX4/glutathione (GSH) axis. Senescent cells had higher basal GSH and elevated GPX4 protein, yet ACase silencing reduced GPX4 expression while still protecting against RSL3-induced cell death. Even when GSH was depleted with buthionine sulfoximine (BSO), ACase knockdown conferred strong resistance to RSL3. The GSH/GPX4 changes therefore appear to be consequences of attenuated ferroptotic pressure rather than the protective mechanism itself, placing ACase upstream of these classic ferroptosis elements.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase) inhibition protects against ferroptosis independently of iron regulation, despite iron being a classic ferroptosis driver via the Fenton reaction. ACase knockdown increased ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1), a buffer of ferrous iron, yet the labile iron pool (LIP, reactive Fe2+) was actually increased in senescent cells after ACase knockdown despite the anti-ferroptotic effect. This demonstrates that ACase inhibition acts upstream of both the GPX4/GSH axis and iron/Fe2+ regulation, protecting cells by reducing the lipid peroxidation substrate pool rather than by modulating iron handling.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase, encoded by ASAH1) is the lysosomal enzyme that breaks down ceramide into sphingosine and free fatty acids. By controlling ceramide levels, ACase affects the abundance of many lipid species relevant to cell fate decisions, including sphingomyelin, ceramide-1-phosphate, and free fatty acids. In the context of replicative senescence, this ceramide catabolism releases free saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that feed polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) and PUFA-phospholipid synthesis, remodeling the membrane lipid profile.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase sensitizes cells to ferroptosis through an entirely novel pathway independent of the mechanisms usually associated with ferroptosis-induced cell death - it does not involve changes in iron or glutathione levels but instead modulates lipid metabolism. This distinguishes it from canonical ferroptosis, which is suppressed by GPX4 and glutathione. Because the acid-ceramidase axis operates through ceramide hydrolysis and membrane PUFA enrichment rather than through GPX4/GSH regulation, it opens a separate druggable route for triggering ferroptosis in senescent cells. First author David Soriano-Castell highlighted this as an entirely novel, GPX4/GSH-independent mechanism.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase breaks down ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids, reshaping membrane lipid composition. In senescent cells, progressively higher expression of this enzyme drives a pro-ferroptotic lipid profile rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids - the preferred substrates for lipid peroxidation. Salk Institute researchers studying human lung cells discovered that elevated acid ceramidase makes senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis and that removal of the enzyme protects both young and old cells from ferroptosis-induced death. Because acid ceramidase inhibitors already exist for other therapeutic purposes, the enzyme represents a druggable target for clearing senescent cells and supporting healthy aging.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase) over-expression increases the polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) content of membrane phospholipids, promoting a pro-ferroptotic lipid profile. Mechanistically, ACase-mediated ceramide breakdown releases free saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that, via the Lands cycle, are exchanged into sn-2 PUFA-containing phospholipids (PL-PUFAs) - the substrates of lipid peroxidation. ACase knockdown in senescent cells decreased the most abundant PL-PUFA species (including PC-AA, PG-DHA, PG-DPA), thereby reducing the lipid peroxidation substrate pool and conferring ferroptosis resistance.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase is a druggable, near-term, testable senotherapeutic target for clearing senescent cells. Experimental drugs targeting acid ceramidase have already been developed for other therapeutic purposes, demonstrating that the enzyme is targetable and lighting the way toward future innovation that could extend healthspans. Because elevated acid ceramidase makes senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis, inhibitors of the enzyme could selectively eliminate senescent 'zombie' cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy. The Salk team calls this a big milestone in the public health effort to support healthy aging, with the next steps being pathway completion, animal translation, and clinical trials.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Senescent cells express progressively higher levels of the enzyme acid ceramidase, and this elevation is mechanistically tied to their heightened vulnerability to ferroptosis. Salk researchers cultured senescent human lung cells, induced ferroptosis, and found they were far more sensitive to this cell death pathway than young, healthy cells, with sensitivity beginning as senescent cells expressed increasingly higher enzyme levels. Removal of acid ceramidase from both senescent and non-senescent cells made them more resilient to induced ferroptosis. The enzyme thus links the two aging-associated cellular programs of senescence and ferroptosis, providing a potential target for removing senescent 'zombie' cells.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase) expression is induced in neighboring proliferative cells by paracrine senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) signaling. Proliferative cells co-cultured with senescent cells (without direct contact) showed a significant time-dependent increase in ACase expression, while ACSL4 was unaffected, and the same effect was observed after incubating proliferative cells with recombinant IL-6/IL-8 (2:1 ratio). This ACase induction by the SASP cytokine IL-6 sensitizes bystander proliferative cells to ferroptosis, providing a mechanism for how senescent cells spread ferroptotic vulnerability through tissue.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase) expression is induced in proliferative cells by paracrine SASP signaling, specifically mediated by the cytokines IL-6 and IL-8. Incubating proliferative cells with recombinant IL-6/IL-8 (2:1 ratio) reproduced the ACase upregulation seen with senescent-cell co-culture, without changing ACSL4. This SASP-driven ACase induction produces senescent-like features - elevated ACase and exacerbated lipid peroxidation - that sensitize neighboring cells to ferroptosis, illustrating how a few senescent cells can spread both senescence and ferroptotic vulnerability through tissue.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: ARN14794 is a specific chemical inhibitor of acid ceramidase (ACase). Treatment with ARN14794 protected proliferative and senescent WI-38 cells, as well as neuronal-derived murine HT22 cells (a well-studied ferroptosis model), against RSL3-induced ferroptosis. Because ACase inhibitors already exist as drug candidates developed for other indications, ACase represents a tractable senolytic/senomorphic target for attenuating the deleterious effects of senescent cells during aging - a potential 'two birds with one stone' strategy that eliminates senescent cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase/ASAH1) is strongly over-expressed in replicatively senescent WI-38 human fibroblasts compared with proliferative cells, with Western blot confirming 5- to 20-fold higher expression. Along with the ferroptosis regulator ACSL4, ACase is among the lipid-metabolism enzymes upregulated in senescence. ACase knockdown reduced its levels strongly in senescent cells (though not fully, consistent with increased stability of ACase in senescence), and the senescence phenotype itself - p21 expression, SA-beta-gal activity, and IL-6/IL-8 secretion - remained intact after knockdown.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase catalyzes the breakdown of ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids, directly producing sphingosine in the cell. This enzymatic hydrolysis is a key branch point in sphingolipid metabolism, and in senescent cells the resulting reshaping of membrane lipid composition pushes membranes toward a pro-ferroptotic profile rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), the preferred substrates for lipid peroxidation. Because the excess sphingosine and free fatty acids generated by elevated acid ceramidase feed the lipid-peroxidation cascade, the enzyme serves as a mechanistic link between the cellular programs of senescence and ferroptosis, and its removal protects cells from ferroptotic death.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Elevated levels of acid ceramidase make senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis, a regulated, iron-dependent cell death pathway driven by toxic accumulation of lipid peroxides. The enzyme promotes ferroptosis by breaking down ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids, reshaping membrane lipid composition toward a pro-ferroptotic profile rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, the preferred substrates for lipid peroxidation. Removing acid ceramidase from cells protected both young and old cells from induced ferroptosis. This represents a novel, GPX4/GSH-independent axis that modulates lipid metabolism rather than iron or glutathione levels, and makes acid ceramidase a promising senolytic target.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase promotes lipid peroxidation by enriching membranes with polyunsaturated fatty acids, the preferred substrates for peroxidative damage. The enzyme breaks down ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids, reshaping membrane lipid composition toward a pro-ferroptotic profile, and lipid peroxides accumulate to toxic levels, driving ferroptotic cell death. Healthy cells normally keep lipid peroxides at steady levels with the help of glutathione, an antioxidant that can stave off ferroptosis, but the acid-ceramidase-driven lipid remodeling shifts the balance toward oxidation. This novel pathway is independent of the usual ferroptosis mechanisms, involving neither changes in iron nor glutathione levels.

subject: Acid ceramidase
context: Acid ceramidase (ACase) upregulation in replicatively senescent cells drives increased sensitivity to ferroptosis, an iron-dependent regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation. Over-expression of ACase amplifies ceramide lipolysis, releasing free saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that are exchanged into sn-2 polyunsaturated fatty acid phospholipids (PL-PUFAs) - the substrates of lipid peroxidation - creating a pro-ferroptotic membrane lipid profile. Conversely, knockdown or chemical inhibition of ACase protects both proliferative and senescent cells against RSL3-induced ferroptosis by decreasing the PL-PUFA substrate pool.

subject: ACLY
context: ACLY (ATP-citrate lyase) catalyzes the downstream conversion of mitochondria-derived citrate exported to the cytosol into acetyl-CoA, the principal substrate for cytosolic acetyl-CoA production and histone acetylation. ACLY expression is increased across multiple senescence models, and its silencing reduces both H3K27ac levels and SASP gene expression in irradiation-induced and replicative senescence. Conversely, citrate supplementation increases histone acetylation and induces pro-inflammatory gene expression in proliferating cells, confirming that increasing citrate availability is sufficient to drive the acetylation-dependent inflammatory programme.

subject: Advanced Glycation End Products
context: Aging is associated with cardiac enlargement and arterial stiffening, and one theory attributes this to an age-related accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). Cross-linking of the proteins that make up the human body plays a role in the human aging process and may be responsible for many problems of old age, including senile cataract, thickening of the arteries, some cancers and damage to the immune system. All the body's proteins deteriorate with advancing age and more so in diabetes, and glycation inhibitors may help alleviate or prevent senile cataract, arterial thickening, kidney failure, thinning bones, osteoarthritis and skin wrinkles.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aging
context: Aging causes drastic architectural changes in the thymus that result in profound tissue involution, dramatic reduction in T cell export, and reduced overall peripheral immunity. Mechanisms are not fully appreciated, and no evolutionary explanation has been confirmed, though hypotheses include energy rechanneling to reproduction once a diverse T cell repertoire is established (Shanley et al.) and promotion of peripheral selection of a well-adapted repertoire (Dowling and Hodgkin). Mouse aging models confirm decreased thymus weight and cellularity with age, with thymocyte number declining steadily across the lifespan.

subject: Aging
context: Aging is the sum of all age-related diseases, pre-diseases and pre-pre-diseases, which limit lifespan, and since humans die from age-related diseases rather than from healthy aging, a drug indicated for all age-related diseases must be an anti-aging drug in that it targets the common driver of these diseases, namely aging itself. Standard medicine extends lifespan mostly by preventing death from overt diseases, extending the unhealthy phase of life, whereas anti-aging medicine increases both healthspan and lifespan and is most effective at the stage of pre-diseases before complications and organ damage occur.

subject: Alagebrium
context: Alagebrium (ALT-711), a thiazolium salt developed by the Alteon Corporation and in stage II trials, is claimed to break existing cross-links rather than merely prevent them. Aminoguanidine and other agents such as carnosine and acetyl-L-carnitine have been shown to help prevent cross-linking, whereas ALT-711 is claimed to break existing links. If this is substantiated, alagebrium could be a major anti-aging medicine of the future, complementing AGE inhibitors that only block formation of new cross-links.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine acts to bind to sugars, thus preventing them from binding to the lysine groups of proteins, which is the mechanism by which it blocks the formation of glucose-derived cross-links. Glucose is found in every cell of the body and is relatively stable, but it can join with protein to form a glucose/protein combination that continues through a number of steps to eventually cause active cross-links. The formation process is reversible, and glycation inhibitors stabilize glucose metabolism, but glucose/protein substances can stay in the body for months or even years, cross-linking with the proteins around them.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine blocks the synthesis of nitric oxide by selectively inhibiting the inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) enzyme, acting upstream of NO signaling in the NO-cGMP vasodilation cascade. While methylene blue blocks NO action downstream at soluble guanylyl cyclase, aminoguanidine prevents the overproduction of NO from the start, during inflammation, injury, or shock. Because it spares the endothelial form of NOS (eNOS), it is considered a theoretical way to halt the inflammatory cascade without shutting down normal blood pressure regulation.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine is a strong inhibitor of diamine oxidase (DAO), the enzyme that breaks down histamine in the gut. By blocking intestinal DAO, oral aminoguanidine can dramatically increase sensitivity to dietary histamine, potentially triggering severe acute histamine intolerance; consuming normal amounts of histamine-rich foods - aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods - may cause headaches, flushing, hives, and tachycardia. This is a major safety consideration for oral aminoguanidine use in supplement or experimental settings.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Trials conducted by the Alteon Corporation indicate that aminoguanidine can significantly reduce albuminuria, proteins present in urine usually as a result of kidney disease, delay the onset of end-stage renal disease, and improve the cholesterol profiles of diabetic patients. Diabetic clinical trials have also highlighted aminoguanidine's ability to prevent oxidative modification of LDL and inhibit the formation of atherosclerotic plaques. A number of studies with diabetic rats indicate that aminoguanidine-administered rats have significantly superior survival rates than untreated animals.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: A number of different studies with diabetic rats indicate that aminoguanidine-administered rats have significantly superior survival rates than untreated animals. Aminoguanidine prolongs survival in azotemic-induced diabetic rats, and it prevents age-related arterial stiffening and cardiac hypertrophy in animals. Human trials indicate aminoguanidine has very low toxicity and appears safe to use at normal dosages, with side effects limited to nausea and headache, although there is still relatively little human data and clinical trials, and broad anti-aging claims rest largely on animal and early human data rather than definitive clinical outcomes.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine prevents the cross-linking of tissue proteins by trapping reactive carbonyl species and by binding to sugars, thus preventing them from binding to the lysine groups of proteins. Glucose can react with protein amino groups in a process called glycation to form glucose/protein combinations that eventually cause active cross-links, and this continuous cross-linking may be prevented by glycation inhibitors whose primary use is to stabilize glucose metabolism. Aminoguanidine joins up with substances that cause links and stops cross-links from developing, protecting the proteins that make up the body from aging damage.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine is a strong inhibitor of diamine oxidase (DAO), the intestinal enzyme that breaks down histamine. By blocking gut DAO, oral aminoguanidine can dramatically increase sensitivity to dietary histamine, potentially triggering severe acute histamine intolerance; consuming normal amounts of histamine-rich foods (aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods) may cause headaches, flushing, hives, and tachycardia. This histamine-sensitivity risk is a major safety consideration for oral use of aminoguanidine.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine (Pimagedine) is primarily known as a selective inhibitor of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), the enzyme responsible for producing high levels of nitric oxide during inflammation. By blocking iNOS, aminoguanidine prevents the overproduction of nitric oxide from the start of the inflammatory cascade, acting upstream of NO signaling. Because it selectively targets the inducible form rather than the healthy endothelial form (eNOS), it is considered a way to halt the inflammatory cascade without completely shutting down normal blood pressure regulation.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine, also developed as pimagedine by Alteon/Synvista Therapeutics, is the first identified inhibitor of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). By trapping reactive carbonyl species, it prevents the cross-linking of tissue proteins that is proposed to drive many features of aging. Most anti-aging research has been carried out using a hydrochloride (HCL) derivative, which is more soluble and less irritating than the bicarbonate form, and aminoguanidine has a half-life of only 4 hours, so dosages of 150-300 mg per day are best administered in split doses.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Trials conducted by the Alteon Corporation indicate that aminoguanidine can significantly reduce albuminuria, delay the onset of end-stage renal disease, and improve the cholesterol profiles of diabetic patients. Diabetic clinical trials have also highlighted aminoguanidine's ability to prevent oxidative modification of LDL and inhibit the formation of atherosclerotic plaques. Together these findings show aminoguanidine acts to improve heart and arterial condition not just by preventing proteins from cross-linking but also by decreasing the AGE-induced cross-linking of the extra-cellular matrix.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine is able to join up with substances that cause links and stop cross-links from developing, and therefore it may help alleviate or prevent senile cataract, thickening of the arteries, kidney failure, thinning bones, osteoarthritis, skin wrinkles and many other signs of aging. One animal study showed that aminoguanidine prevented age-related cardiac enlargement, reduced the membrane surface area of the rats by 30%, and increased the collagen content of their arterial walls by 24-30%, improving overall heart and arterial condition by decreasing AGE-induced cross-linking of the extracellular matrix.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine prevents the formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), which are implicated in diabetic complications such as damage to blood vessels and kidneys. Under the developmental name Pimagedine, it was evaluated in phase III clinical trials for diabetic nephropathy but was ultimately not approved for widespread clinical use due to safety concerns, including a risk of autoimmune reactions and vitamin B6 depletion. Today it remains primarily an experimental tool, and its AGE-inhibiting activity underlies its study for long-term, chronic conditions in diabetics.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine has the potential to slow the aging process by protecting the proteins that make up the human body, such as the skin proteins collagen and elastin, eye lens protein, nerve protein and kidney proteins, from aging damage. One animal study showed aminoguanidine increased the collagen content of arterial walls by 24-30%, and it decreases AGE-induced cross-linking of the extracellular matrix. Aminoguanidine is able to combat some of the adverse effects of diabetes and improve the quality and duration of life, protecting proteins that deteriorate with advancing age and more so in diabetes.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Studies conducted at the University of Milan over 25 years showed that aminoguanidine reduces the ability of very low density lipoprotein (VLDL), the bad form of cholesterol, to bind itself to blood vessel walls, in tests on animals. In turn, blood platelets are less likely to coagulate and form dangerous clots. Aminoguanidine's role in reducing VLDL cholesterol and its ability to stabilize glucose metabolism indicate it has a wide-reaching ability to help prevent and treat a number of aging disorders.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine selectively inhibits only the inducible form of nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) rather than the healthy endothelial form (eNOS). This selectivity is considered advantageous because it can halt the inflammatory overproduction of nitric oxide - which causes excessive vasodilation, vascular leakage, and tissue damage - without completely shutting down normal blood-pressure regulation maintained by eNOS-derived NO. This contrasts with non-selective NOS inhibition, making aminoguanidine a theoretically more targeted anti-inflammatory intervention.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine, under the developmental name Pimagedine, was evaluated in phase III clinical trials for diabetic nephropathy as a long-term chronic therapy aimed at preventing the slow, progressive formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) that damage blood vessels and kidneys in diabetics. It was ultimately not approved for widespread clinical use due to safety concerns, including a risk of autoimmune reactions and vitamin B6 depletion. Today it is primarily used as an experimental tool in laboratory settings.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine has an ability to treat patients whose blood vessels are constricted by atherosclerosis. In 1992 at the University of Milan, 11 patients with peripheral vascular disease were treated with aminoguanidine; their blood vessels were so clogged they could not walk for more than 500 yards, but after treatment blood flow improved on average by 30% and exercise abilities improved by 50% to 105%. Diabetic clinical trials also highlighted aminoguanidine's ability to prevent oxidative modification of LDL and inhibit the formation of atherosclerotic plaques.
source_document: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md

subject: Androgen Receptor
context: Intracellular androgen receptors (iARs) are expressed in both male and female thymus, in thymic stromal cells and in all thymocyte subsets. Studies by Olsen and colleagues suggest that the significant enlargement of the thymus seen in castrated rodents is mediated by androgen receptor signaling: the AR pathway transduces the pro-involutionary effects of sex steroids on the thymus. Thymic regeneration following castration is reversed in a dose-dependent manner by administration of testosterone or estrogen, consistent with receptor-mediated suppression of thymopoiesis.

subject: Antioxidants
context: Antioxidants did not extend lifespan in any clinical trials and were detrimental in some: in two very large randomized controlled trials, antioxidants increased the incidence of cancer, especially lung cancer in smokers, and increased all-cause mortality, leading both trials to be stopped earlier than planned. Antioxidants also accelerate cancer progression and promote metastasis. The idea that free radicals cause aging was based on circumstantial evidence, and although excessive ROS can shorten lifespan, organisms normally die from mTOR-driven age-related diseases before ROS can kill them, so antioxidant supplementation is described as worse than useless for life extension.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin improved cognitive and affective outcomes in prematurely aged mice following whole-body irradiation: Y-maze spontaneous alternation tests showed basic recovery of short-term working memory in apigenin-treated aged animals, and open-field assays showed prolonged exploration of the central zone, indicating reduced anxiety-like behavior. These findings suggest that SASP suppression by apigenin can counteract neurobehavioral deficits associated with premature aging.

subject: Apigenin
context: In C57BL/6J mice prematurely aged by sublethal whole-body irradiation (WBI), intraperitoneal apigenin partially but significantly reversed physical dysfunction and improved exercise performance: grip strength, hanging endurance, rotarod duration and balance-beam crossing were all restored relative to vehicle. Apigenin also reversed WBI-associated graying fur and age-related expansion of pulmonary alveoli, and improved spleen white pulp architecture.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin directly binds peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6), identified as its bona fide molecular target through two affinity-based approaches: biotin-tagged apigenin pull-down (Bio-APIG) and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS). Binding was confirmed by cellular thermal shift assay, surface plasmon resonance (KD ~ 0.237 uM) and microscale thermophoresis (Kd ~ 916 nM). In silico modelling indicates direct hydrogen bonds with Cys91 and Glu210 of PRDX6; mutating either residue weakens binding ~10-fold and mutating both abolishes it. This is the primary upstream molecular interaction underlying apigenin's senomorphic activity.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin prevents progression of the acute stress-associated phenotype (ASAP) into the chronic, pro-inflammatory SASP. The ASAP is the immediate cellular reaction to genotoxic or environmental insult, characterized by ATM phosphorylation and nucleus-to-cytoplasm translocation, TRAF6 auto-ubiquitination and TAK1 activation, occurring before senescence markers become evident. Under bleomycin stress, TAK1 phosphorylation and subsequent p38 MAPK activation and PI3K/Akt/mTOR engagement normally sustain the secretory phenotype. Apigenin leaves ATM and TAK1 phosphorylation largely intact but blocks downstream transduction through HSPA8, halting the ASAP-to-SASP switch.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin halts cell cycle progression in cancer cells at either the G1 or G2/M phase depending on the cell type. In breast, colon, bladder, and lung cancer cells it induces G2/M arrest associated with decreased cyclin B1 and CDK1 (cdc2) expression and kinase activity, whereas in prostate and cervical cells it produces G1 arrest with reduced cyclin D, E and CDK2/4/6 levels. These blocks are linked to induction of the CDK inhibitors p21/Waf1 and p27/Kip1, inhibition of Rb phosphorylation, and can occur through both p53-dependent and p53-independent pathways.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: In HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells, apigenin induces apoptosis through proteasomal degradation of the HER2/neu oncoprotein, depleting HER2 protein in vivo and consequently inhibiting its auto-phosphorylation and transphosphorylation. This suppresses the HER2/HER3-PI3K/Akt survival cascade and results in cytochrome c release, GADD45 upregulation, and apoptosis, with minimal toxicity toward normal cells. Apigenin's anti-proliferative efficacy is significantly greater in cells overexpressing HER2/neu than in cells expressing basal HER2 levels, and it additionally inhibits STAT3 signaling in HER2-positive lines.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin specifically abrogates the interaction of HSPA8 (heat shock cognate protein 70, HSC70), a shared interactor of both ATM and p38 MAPK identified from proteome-scale interactor profiling (19 proteins shared by ATM and p38 MAPK). Co-immunoprecipitation shows that apigenin attenuates HSPA8's direct binding to p-ATM and to p38 MAPK, whereas the related interactor NPM1 is unaffected, demonstrating target specificity. HSPA8 is a chaperone involved in chaperone-mediated autophagy and NF-κB activation, and its inhibition with the selective drug VER155008 phenocopies apigenin's dampening of SASP factors, p38 MAPK activation, and PI3K/Akt engagement.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin has inherently poor bioavailability that restricts its clinical translation. It is unstable, poorly soluble in water and organic solvents, and after oral intake is rapidly metabolized via UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A1) into glucuronide and sulfate conjugates that are quickly transported in blood and excreted in bile or urine, so plasma apigenin levels are often unmeasurable. In rats, radiolabeled apigenin distributed widely with only 51 percent of radioactivity recovered in urine, and blood levels showed a long elimination half-time of 91.8 hours. This slow pharmacokinetics may permit tissue accumulation for chemopreventive effects, and nano-formulations and beta-glycoside forms are being explored to improve delivery.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: A central mechanism of apigenin's anticancer activity is the induction of apoptosis in a wide range of human cancer cell lines including breast, colon, gastric, pancreatic, prostate, cervical, hematologic, thyroid, neuroblastoma, bladder, and osteosarcoma cells. Apigenin triggers both the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, through loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, cytochrome c release, and activation of caspases 3, 7, 8 and 9, and the extrinsic pathway involving death receptors and TRAIL. Apoptosis is typically dose- and time-dependent, and its potency in leukemia cells ranked higher than other flavonoids tested.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Beyond apoptosis, apigenin induces autophagic cell death in several cancer models, most notably in aggressive breast cancer cells where apigenin-induced autophagy occurs simultaneously with apoptosis. In papillary thyroid cancer, apigenin-induced cell death involves autophagy, likely driven by ROS stimulation, DNA damage, and G2/M phase cell cycle arrest. Combination studies show that blocking autophagy can either enhance (breast cancer) or suppress (neuroblastoma with 4-HPR) apigenin's pro-apoptotic action, indicating context-dependent crosstalk between the two death programs in determining the net anticancer effect.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin is a potent inhibitor of casein kinase 2 (CK2), a serine/threonine kinase that is elevated in many cancers. In prostate cancer, apigenin inhibited CK2 activity in both hormone-responsive LNCaP and hormone-refractory PC-3 cells, though apoptosis was induced only in LNCaP. In colon cancer cells, apigenin together with DRB inhibited CK2 expression and synergistically sensitized cells to TNF-alpha-mediated apoptosis. In cervical cancer stem-like cells, apigenin suppressed self-renewal by downregulating CK2-alpha, and in pancreatic cancer it stabilized the transcription factor Ikaros by downregulating CK2 to restore T-cell homeostasis.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin suppresses cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), the enzyme that converts arachidonic acid into prostaglandins and whose overexpression drives carcinogenesis. It inhibits UVB-induced increases in COX-2 protein and mRNA in mouse and human keratinocytes, reduces COX-2 expression in colon and gastric cancer models, and downregulates inducible COX-2 in HCEC colon cells more potently than quercetin or tricin. In non-melanoma skin cancer models, COX-2 inhibition by apigenin prevents tumor development, and apigenin also suppresses UVB-induced cutaneous angiogenesis by maintaining endogenous TSP1 levels.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin inhibits fatty acid synthase (FASN), an enzyme that catalyzes long-chain fatty acid synthesis and is overexpressed in many cancers. Brusselmans and colleagues showed that plant flavonoids including apigenin induce apoptosis in prostate and breast carcinoma cells specifically through their ability to block fatty acid synthase activity, and this effect on lipogenesis was also observed in osteosarcoma cells where apigenin and luteolin downregulated FASN and acetyl-CoA carboxylase. By depriving cancer cells of de novo lipid synthesis, apigenin curbs cancer cell growth and survival through a metabolic route complementary to its effects on signaling kinases.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin acts as a histone deacetylase inhibitor, directly targeting HDAC1 and HDAC3, which increases global histone acetylation and produces localized hyperacetylation of histone H3 on the p21/Waf1 promoter. In triple-negative breast cancer cells this drives histone H3 acetylation, decreasing cyclin A and cyclin B and increasing p21/Waf1/Cip1. Apigenin can additionally function as a dual epigenetic inhibitor that reverses both DNA methylation and trimethylation of lysine 27 on histone H3, qualifying it as an epigenetic modulator relevant to chemoprevention.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin decreases hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1alpha) protein but not the HIF-1beta subunit, acting at the HIF-1alpha binding site to suppress transcriptional activation of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and downstream angiogenesis. In lung cancer A549 cells and xenografts, apigenin at 15 uM reduced tumor volume partly by inhibiting the HIF-1alpha-VEGF pathway, and it also blocked AKT and p70S6K1 activation that mediates VEGF transcription. The same HIF-1alpha/VEGF suppression was observed in pancreatic and ovarian cancer cells under both hypoxic and normoxic conditions, establishing anti-angiogenesis as a core anticancer mechanism.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin modulates the MAPK cascade, inducing dose-dependent phosphorylation of ERK and p38 while having little effect on JNK phosphorylation in colon carcinoma and keratinocyte models. It also suppresses MEKK1-driven activation of ERK, JNK, and p38 in bladder smooth-muscle cells, thereby inhibiting cell migration and actin polymerization. In thyroid cancer cells apigenin disrupted EGFR tyrosine auto-phosphorylation and downstream MAPK signaling. Its net effect on the MAPK axis contributes to its chemopreventive activity by restraining proliferation, migration, and invasion across multiple cancer types.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin suppresses NF-kB signaling, a ubiquitous transcription factor controlling cell survival, apoptosis, and immune function. In gastric cancer cells infected with Helicobacter pylori, apigenin inhibited NF-kB activation and downstream inflammatory mediators including COX-2, ICAM-1, IL-6, IL-8, and ROS. In prostate cancer cells apigenin downregulated nuclear expression of NF-kB p65 and p50 while upregulating cytosolic IkBalpha, and in pancreatic and mesothelioma models it restricted NF-kB DNA binding and attenuated NF-kB-dependent survival, sensitizing tumors to apoptosis and to gemcitabine or TRAIL combination therapy.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin is a well-characterized inhibitor of the PI3K/Akt survival pathway across multiple cancer types. It directly blocks PI3K activity, which in turn inhibits Akt function, and this is particularly consequential in HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells where PI3K/Akt signaling sustains cell survival. Downstream consequences of PI3K/Akt suppression by apigenin include reduced p-Akt (Ser473 and Thr308), activation of FOXO3a leading to increased BIM and p27/Kip1, decreased VEGF expression, and restored sensitivity to apoptosis, contributing to both growth inhibition and anti-metastatic effects in prostate, lung, ovarian, and pancreatic models.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin inhibits STAT3 signaling in HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells, exerting anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic activity and positioning it as a potential preventive agent. Downstream of STAT3 inhibition, apigenin down-regulates STAT3 target genes involved in migration and invasion, including MMP-2, MMP-9, VEGF, and Twist1. This STAT3-suppressive activity complements apigenin's broader multikinase profile, which also targets PI3K/Akt, MAPK, Src, and CK2, reinforcing its role as a pleiotropic anticancer agent rather than a single-pathway drug.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Among PRDX6's three enzymatic activities (peroxidase, acidic calcium-independent phospholipase A2 / aiPLA2, and lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase), apigenin selectively suppresses the iPLA2 activity. Unlike NAC, a selective peroxidase inhibitor (IC50 = 15.5 µM for H2O2 clearance), apigenin only modestly impairs H2O2 scavenging (IC50 = 49.5 µM), indicating its SASP-dampening effect does not depend on peroxidase function. Instead, blocking the PLA2 arm of PRDX6 curbs production of pro-inflammatory arachidonic acid and downstream signaling.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin (4',5,7-trihydroxyflavone) is a naturally occurring flavone belonging to the class of dietary flavonoids found in fruits and vegetables. It is historically recognized for antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antiviral and anticancer activities, and it reduces reactive oxygen species production while raising glutathione and mitochondrial ATP to protect oocyte quality during aging. Its canonical downstream anti-inflammatory actions include suppressing the SASP partially by inhibiting IL-1α signaling through IRAK1/IRAK4, p38 MAPK and NF-κB, which reduces the aggressiveness of human breast cancer cells.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin (4',5,7-trihydroxyflavone) is a major plant flavone belonging to the flavonoid subclass flavones within the polyphenols. It is a yellow crystalline powder with the molecular formula C15H10O5 and a molecular weight of 270.24 Da, bearing hydroxyl groups at C-5 and C-7 of the A-ring and C-4' of the B-ring. Structurally it is related to biapigenin and naturally occurs as apigenin-7-O-glucoside and acylated derivatives. Its classification as a flavone underpins its shared antioxidant and anti-inflammatory pharmacology with other plant polyphenols such as quercetin and kaempferol.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin is a dietary flavone flavonoid identified by screening a 66-compound natural product library against bleomycin-senescent PSC27 human prostate stromal cells. It functions as a senomorphic agent: it suppresses the pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) without killing senescent cells or forcing them back into the cell cycle, in contrast to senolytics such as ABT-263 or procyanidin C1, which preferentially lyse senescent cells. Because it leaves the growth arrest intact, apigenin is classified specifically as a natural senomorphic rather than a senolytic, aligning with the ideal profile for SASP-restraining geroprotective therapy.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin is a major dietary flavone enriched in a range of fruits and vegetables, with parsley being the richest documented source. Dried parsley was reported to contain up to 45,035 ug/g apigenin, far exceeding dried chamomile flowers (3,000-5,000 ug/g), celery seeds (786.5 ug/g), vine spinach (622 ug/g), and Chinese celery (240.2 ug/g). It is also found in chamomile tea, red wine, and beer, and is a signature component of the Mediterranean diet, whose intake has been associated epidemiologically with lower rates of several human diseases including cancer.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: In the intestine and liver, apigenin is extensively conjugated by UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 (UGT1A1), the key enzyme converting it into glucuronide and sulfate derivatives that are more readily transported in blood and excreted in bile or urine, and apigenin itself induces UGT1A1 transcription in colon cells. Combined treatment with sulforaphane synergistically increased UGT1A1 mRNA induction, although apigenin did not induce GSTA1. This phase II metabolism underlies apigenin's rapid clearance and low plasma bioavailability after oral dosing, while its slow systemic elimination may allow peripheral tissue accumulation that supports chemopreventive efficacy.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin is not senolytic and does not reverse cellular senescence: SA-β-Gal staining profiles and mitotic inactivity remain essentially unchanged in senescent cells treated with apigenin, both in vitro and in xenografts and whole-body-irradiated mouse tissues. It also fails to downregulate the core senescence markers p16^INK4a and p21^CIP1 in vivo. Instead of eliminating senescent cells, apigenin curtails their pathological secretory output. This property is considered pharmacologically favorable because rejuvenating or removing cells is not required to blunt the harmful paracrine effects of the SASP, and retained senescent cells may still contribute beneficial functions such as t...

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin markedly increases the efficacy of several chemotherapeutic drugs when combined, by blocking survival signaling and resensitizing resistant or stem-cell populations. Pretreatment with low-dose apigenin followed by cisplatin, 5-fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, or gemcitabine produced greater growth inhibition of pancreatic cancer cells than either agent alone. Apigenin sensitized doxorubicin-resistant BEL-7402 cells by raising intracellular doxorubicin, overcame MRP1-mediated resistance in ovarian carcinoma, synergized with curcumin to depolymerize microtubules in lung cancer cells, and combined with cisplatin to kill CD44-positive prostate cancer stem cells. These effects typically involve suppression of PI3K/Akt and NF-kB together with induction of apoptosis.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: Epidemiologic and case-control studies support an inverse relationship between apigenin-containing flavonoid intake and the risk of several cancers, including ovarian cancer. A multi-centric Italian case-control study of 1,031 epithelial ovarian cancer cases and 2,411 controls confirmed an inverse association between consumption of common flavonoids and ovarian cancer risk, and a Zutphen study established that dietary supplementation of five flavonoids including apigenin decreased ovarian cancer risk. Similar protective associations were reported for breast, gastric, and colorectal cancers, with a 5-year follow-up of elderly subjects concluding that high fruit-and-vegetable flavonoid intake reduces cancer incidence.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: In a preclinical NOD-SCID xenograft model combining PC3 prostate cancer cells with senescent PSC27 stroma, co-administration of apigenin with the chemotherapy agent mitoxantrone (MIT) produced additional tumor reduction beyond MIT alone: MIT alone shrank tumors 57.8%, and the combination achieved an additional 51.1% reduction, for a total 74.9% decrease versus placebo. Apigenin reversed circulating SASP factors (amphiregulin/AREG, epiregulin/EREG) and enhanced DNA damage (γH2AX) and cleaved-caspase-3 apoptosis in tumors.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin stabilizes and activates the tumor suppressor p53, which contributes importantly to its cancer-preventive effects. In pancreatic cancer cells apigenin enhanced acetylation of p53 at lysine 382, increasing nuclear translocation and DNA binding, while also restoring function to mutant p53. In cervical and bladder cancer cells apigenin induced p53-dependent apoptosis with upregulation of p21/Waf1 and Fas/APO-1, and in keratinocytes it caused p53 accumulation with p21 induction. Importantly, apigenin also induces p21/Waf1 through p53-independent routes in p53-mutant cells, so its growth-inhibitory action does not strictly depend on p53 status.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Apigenin
context: At a minimally optimal concentration of 10 µM, apigenin dose-dependently decreases a broad set of canonical SASP factors including IL-6, IL-8/CXCL8, IL-1α, IL-1β, MMP1/MMP3, GM-CSF, TIMP1 and WNT16B, both at transcript and protein level across senescent PSC27, WI38 and IMR90 cells regardless of senescence-inducing modality (replicative, oncogene-induced, or therapy-induced) or organ origin. GSEA shows suppression of SASP and NF-κB signatures; KEGG analysis reveals inhibition of TNF and NF-κB signaling, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, and type I interferon pathways. Crucially, SA-β-Gal positivity and mitotic arrest remain unchanged, confirming SASP-selective senomorphic action.

subject: Apigenin
context: Apigenin consistently induces the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21/Waf1/Cip1 across cancer models, which mediates its cell-cycle-arrest and pro-apoptotic effects. In prostate LNCaP cells p21 is induced in a p53-dependent manner alongside p27/Kip1, whereas in p53-mutant colon and osteosarcoma cells apigenin still elevated p21/Waf1 in a dose- and time-dependent manner via a p53-independent pathway. Apigenin also functions as an HDAC inhibitor that increases global histone acetylation and hyperacetylates histone H3 specifically at the p21/Waf1 promoter, directly driving p21 transcription in triple-negative breast cancer cells.
source_document: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md

subject: Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor
context: Kynurenine and its derivatives activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), which promotes regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation while suppressing effector T and NK cells. This is a central effector arm of IDO1-mediated immunosuppression: IDO1 in antigen-presenting cells such as dendritic cells depletes local tryptophan and produces kynurenine, creating an immunosuppressive microenvironment that favors immune tolerance. This pathway underlies IDO1's physiological roles in maternal-fetal tolerance, regulation of inflammation and autoimmunity, antimicrobial defense, and tumor immune escape, where IDO1 is often upregulated in cancers and the tumor microenvironment.

subject: Aspirin
context: Aspirin not only reduces inflammation, a hallmark of aging, it also reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease, thrombosis and cancer; low-dose aspirin prevents one-third of colorectal, gastric and esophageal cancers. Millions of people take aspirin daily to prevent cardiovascular disease and cancer, and it was calculated that the benefits of aspirin are greater than its risks despite side effects including life-threatening gastric bleeding. The author argues that the benefits of the anti-aging effects of rapamycin and everolimus may be even greater, and that aspirin can be combined with rapamycin in an anti-aging formulation.

subject: ATFS-1
context: ATFS-1 (Activating Transcription Factor associated with Stress-1) is the transcription factor required for activation of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) in C. elegans. Uniquely, it possesses both a mitochondrial targeting sequence and a nuclear localization signal: in the absence of stress it is imported into mitochondria and rapidly degraded, whereas under mitochondrial dysfunction its import is impaired and it translocates to the nucleus to orchestrate a broad transcriptional response, including induction of mitochondrial chaperones. Nuclear ATFS-1 thereby couples mitochondrial status directly to nuclear gene expression.

subject: ATFS-1
context: In C. elegans, mitochondrial dysfunction caused by protein misfolding alters the subcellular localization of the transcription factor ATFS-1. In healthy mitochondria, ATFS-1 is imported into the organelle and degraded by the Lon protease. During stress, ATFS-1 instead traffics to the nucleus to drive transcription of genes involved in the coordinated UPRmt response. This import-versus-nuclear-translocation decision makes protein import a readout of mitochondrial health, a paradigm the review argues is extended in mammals by mechanisms involving DELE1 processing and PINK1 accumulation.

subject: Autophagy
context: Rapamycin's geroprotective effects are often attributed to autophagy induction, yet autophagy has dual, context-dependent roles in cancer: while it may suppress tumor initiation by clearing damaged cellular components, it can also support the survival and growth of established tumors by providing substrates for metabolism and clearing damage that would otherwise be lethal. Thus enhancing autophagy in aging populations with elevated cancer risks and an unknown genetic background may inadvertently promote oncogenesis.
source_document: _document_ - Rapamycin for longevity the pros, the cons, and future perspectives.md

subject: Biphasic Dose-Response Curve
context: For a network to produce a biphasic dose-response curve, the probability is highly increased if one of the bivalent interactions of the inhibited target operates in the saturated enzymatic regime, i.e., a Michaelis-Menten interaction with high affinity towards its substrate whose reaction speed does not depend on substrate amount. Specifically, the Michaelis-Menten constant K21 of the backward interaction from Target to Input must be significantly low. Fixing K21 to a low value raises the percentage of hormetic parameter sets from about 6% to 80%, a roughly ten-fold increase in the probability of observing hormesis.

subject: BNIP3
context: BNIP3 (BCL-2/adenovirus E1B interacting protein 3) is an outer mitochondrial membrane mitophagy receptor that interacts directly with LC3 to promote engulfment of damaged mitochondria, functioning independently of Parkin. NIX/BNIP3-mediated mitophagy is induced through hypoxia and stabilization of HIF-1alpha. BNIP3 also interacts with OPA1 to induce mitochondrial fragmentation and with FUNDC1 under the control of OPA1 and DRP1, and its protein levels are upregulated at early premalignant stages of several human solid cancers but frequently decrease when tumors become invasive.
source_document: _document_ - The role of mitochondrial dynamics in disease.md

subject: Branched-Chain Amino Acids
context: High circulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) levels - leucine, isoleucine, and valine - are associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and mortality in humans. High-BCAA diets promote obesity, insulin resistance, inflammation, and decreased lifespan in rodents, whereas dietary restriction of BCAAs promotes metabolic health, reduces frailty, and extends lifespan, recapitulating many benefits of protein restriction. BCAA restriction reduces mTORC1 signaling, induces Fgf21, reduces hepatic cellular senescence, and in human studies improves insulin sensitivity and glucose/insulin homeostasis while increasing circulating FGF21. Although BCAAs are often considered as a group, each individual BCAA plays distinct roles in aging.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: Caloric restriction (CR) and intermittent fasting extend both lifespan and healthspan in diverse species, but CR is of little benefit when started in old age and fasting inhibits the mTOR pathway in young but not old mice. By contrast, rapamycin strongly inhibits mTORC1 at any age and extends lifespan whether started late or early in life. The beneficial effects of rapamycin and CR may be additive since they are exerted through overlapping but distinct mechanisms, and intermittent rapamycin and CR can be combined, with exercise potentially most beneficial immediately after rapamycin use.

subject: CD38
context: CD38 becomes hyperactive with age and hydrolyzes NAD+ into ADPR, contributing to age-related NAD+ depletion, calcium imbalance, mitochondrial fragmentation, and oxidative stress. Alongside PARP1 and SARM1, CD38 is a major NAD+-consuming enzyme driving the decline in NAD+ availability during aging. Because reduced NAD+ compromises SIRT1 and SIRT3 activity and triggers mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence (MiDAS) via AMPK-p53 signaling, CD38 hyperactivity is a key mechanistic contributor to the metabolic bottleneck that links declining NAD+ to stem cell exhaustion and impaired resilience. CD38 is therefore considered a target for NAD+-boosting strategies.
source_document: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md

subject: Cellular Senescence
context: Senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions, including osteoarthritis, poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, according to senior author Pam Maher. The harmful factors senescent cells release (the SASP) promote tissue dysfunction and disease development in surrounding tissue. Because senescence and ferroptosis are both independently linked to age-related dysfunction, the discovery that elevated acid ceramidase makes senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis offers a two-birds-with-one-stone strategy: eliminating senescent cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy. Clearing senescent cells is considered a promising therapeutic approach for a multitude of age-related diseases and disorders.

subject: Cellular Senescence
context: Senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions, including osteoarthritis (arthritis), poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's or Parkinson's. The pro-inflammatory factors that senescent cells secrete into surrounding tissues promote tissue dysfunction and disease development, contributing to the joint degeneration seen in arthritis. The Salk findings suggest that making senescent cells vulnerable to ferroptosis through acid ceramidase could provide a novel target for therapeutics applicable to a multitude of diseases and disorders, including arthritis. Senescent cells are considered a hallmark of aging, and clearing them is a major goal of senolytic research for extending healthspan.

subject: Cellular Senescence
context: Senescent cells can promote the development of diseases or disorders, including cancer, through the harmful factors they release into surrounding tissues (the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, or SASP). Though sometimes harmless, senescent cells that accumulate with age produce a pro-inflammatory environment that supports tumor development and age-related tissue dysfunction. This is why senescent cells are a hallmark of aging and why strategies to clear them - for example, via the acid ceramidase/ferroptosis axis - are pursued as senolytic approaches. Senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions including arthritis, poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases.
source_document: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md

subject: Cellular Senescence
context: Senescent cells - often called 'zombie' cells - are a hallmark of aging: they do not completely die but also are not quite alive, and while sometimes harmless, they release harmful factors called the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) into surrounding tissues. This secretory phenotype is pro-inflammatory and can promote the development of diseases or disorders, including cancer, and accelerates aging by driving tissue dysfunction. Because senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions including arthritis, poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, clearing them - as proposed through acid ceramidase-mediated ferroptosis sensitization - is a major strategy for extending healthspan.
source_document: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md

subject: Cellular Senescence
context: Vulnerable senescent cells are able to pass their ferroptosis vulnerability on to neighboring cells, helping explain why only a few senescent cells can turn into more and ultimately impact a larger tissue over time. This paracrine transmission of ferroptosis sensitivity means that a small number of senescent cells can spread susceptibility to ferroptotic death across a tissue, and it represents one mechanism by which the Salk team found ferroptosis and senescence to be connected during aging. The researchers describe the target as eliminating senescent cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy for longer, and the finding underpins the therapeutic rationale for targeting acid ceramidase.

subject: cGAS-STING Pathway
context: mtDNA-cGAS-STING signalling and mitochondrial control of histone acetylation operate as independently regulated pathways: senescent BAX- and BAK-deficient fibroblasts show reduced SASP gene expression from impaired cytosolic mtDNA release yet unchanged H3K27ac at SASP loci, and STING inhibition suppresses SASP without affecting histone acetylation. Despite this independence the pathways functionally cooperate: disruption of either is sufficient to suppress SASP while activation of either alone is not sufficient to fully restore it. Acetyl-CoA enables chromatin accessibility at SASP loci while mtDNA-driven innate immune signalling provides the activation required to engage these regions.
